title: Fukuoka Jisho Deploys Netskope Across Seven Group Companies to Deliver Secure Access Anywhere, Powered by SSE
summary: Fukuoka Jisho Co., Ltd., guided by its philosophy of “For an Exciting Fukuoka,” leads redevelopment and urban development projects including Canal City Hakata. The company’s DX Promotion Department, which manages IT infrastructure for seven group companies including subsidiaries, decided to move away from perimeter-based defense — which trusted connections based on location and destination — toward zero trust. It adopted Netskope as its cloud-first SSE (Security Service Edge) solution, using a single, consistent policy to gain visibility into and control over access to cloud services, the web, and internal systems. After restructuring its partner arrangement to establish stable operations, and carefully accounting for the needs of varied business lines such as its hotel operations, Fukuoka Jisho rolled out the platform across all seven group companies while minimizing disruption. Today, the company maintains the same level of security and convenience regardless of where employees work.
body_markdown:
From an operations perspective, Fukuoka Jisho retired its VPN — which carried vulnerability risk and was cumbersome to connect to — along with the legacy mechanism for reaching file servers from outside the network, and now manages access control policy centrally through Netskope. “We’ve seen fewer inquiries about accessing internal systems, and users no longer have to deal with connecting to a VPN,” Nishikubo says.


From a user’s perspective, there are no longer systems that only work from inside the office; employees can access Box, Microsoft 365, and other services the same way regardless of location. “Success, for us, is that users can keep working without having to think about it,” Nishikubo says. “We’ve also stopped getting questions about how to access internal systems from outside.”


At the same time, greater visibility under zero trust means more to keep an eye on. “With perimeter-based defense, there was a single line to defend,” Nishikubo notes. “With zero trust, every device and service needs continuous verification and authorization, so the number of places we need to watch multiplies.” This is, in part, the result of being able to see risks that were previously difficult to detect. Fukuoka Jisho is addressing the resulting increase in monitoring and operational work through its partner’s managed services.


Looking ahead, the company’s focus is on balancing the use of generative AI with security governance. Fukuoka Jisho already provides several generative AI services to all employees. “We want to think more concretely about how to manage AI agents as non-human identities,” Terashi says. Kitahara, for his part, would like to see better searchability for technical documentation tailored to specific use cases, clearer guidance on which features are available under the company’s current licenses, and an environment where the impact of policy changes can be safely tested.


Fukuoka Jisho will continue to advance its security foundation, built around Netskope One SSE, to support the growth of the diverse businesses behind its urban development work.
